independentAttacksBeyondDispatch.attack: The NT-3 fixture carries a second, independent fault: FactCandidateV1 is a closed type requiring canonicalRelationPayload, and the fixture omits it while adding two unknown fields (canonicalRelationPayloadHex, decodedRelationPayload). Under wireSchema.canonicalCbor.decodeRule, missing and unknown fields are provider-protocol, so a conforming host would refuse at decode and never reach the relation-registry check the fixture claims to isolate — the same class of defect Codex raised as G23FXV2-M1 against the NT-5 members.
independentAttacksBeyondDispatch.evidence: This is not an invention of the corpus; it is the host contract's own JSON transcription convention. fact-plane.v1's conformance vector fact-id-v1-typescript-declares — the vector the subject pins and which delivery.v2 FactCandidateV1.factRecordJoin names as its conformanceVectorId — carries candidate fields spelled exactly canonicalRelationPayloadHex plus decodedRelationPayload, because a CBOR byte string has no native JSON form. I decoded the fixture's hex and re-encoded decodedRelationPayload under deterministic CBOR: they round-trip exactly, so the transcription is faithful and the wire object it denotes does carry a conforming canonicalRelationPayload. The subject's phrasing is precise rather than evasive: 'No canonicalRelationPayload field' describes the JSON transcription, and doesNot 'Does not put hex text in canonicalRelationPayload' is the guarantee that matters. The fixture is byte-identical to the v2 fixture (diff clean), matching the subject's claim 'NT-3 JSON vector unchanged from v2 except path', and its sole divergence from the pinned host vector is relationSchemaId 'opensip.relation.declares.v1' → 'provider.minted.not-host-owned'. One mutation, correctly isolated.

decision: ACCEPT — 0 blockers, 0 MUST-FIX, 0 SHOULD-FIX. Both v2 MUST-FIX findings and the one v2 SHOULD-FIX are landed, and each was verified by recomputation rather than by reading the subject's claim. Codex G23FXV2-M1 is landed with the domain separator now present and all three coverageCommitments reproducing bit-exactly under the pinned domainRule — two of the three equal the very values the rejecting review computed as required, and the third differs only because the Claude M1 repair changed that fixture's entries. Claude M1 is landed twice over: the narrows fixture no longer converts unknown to covered, and hostRequestedCoverageBaseline is now declared on all three Coverage members, which converts the EV-2/EV-3 separation from prose into an arithmetic property. Claude S1 is landed and the selector resolves. I attacked the NT-3 member as carrying an independent decode-time fault and refuted my own attack against fact-plane.v1's conformance vector, which uses the same hex-plus-decoded transcription; the fixture is byte-identical to v2 and its sole divergence from the pinned vector is the intended relationSchemaId mutation. Custody is exact: subject and all four fixtures unmoved at 0444, both frozen predecessors unmoved, all 19 recorded digests and all three cited commits verified against live bytes. The artifact binds nothing, applies nothing, closes no leftover-design, and correctly declines to be a SATISFIED-GRADE act under D-056 gate 2.
